content.text: The evidence is clear: io-pay (third-party, IO Payments Ltd) started returning 503s, and error rate/latency spiked in lockstep at 17:58. No deployment changes were found in the lookback windows already checked. This is an upstream dependency failure.

hypotheses.subject: io-pay
hypotheses.summary: io-pay, the third-party payment provider io-shop calls while rendering the account page, began returning 503 errors at 17:58:00Z. This matches the onset exactly - error rate and latency (p50/p95/p99) jumped in the same minute the PaymentProviderFailed errors began, and stayed elevated. Since IO Payments Ltd is a third-party owned by another company, io-shop cannot restart or revert anything to fix it.

supporting_evidence.claim: ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - PaymentProviderFailed: api.io-pay.example returned 503 for /v1/shoppers/shopper-19845-4-0/card at src/io_shop/payment_provider.py:96
WARN io-shop: account page error rate at 100.00% over the last minute
io-pay: third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd, at api.io-pay.example - Holds the card Io charges. Called while the account page renders, because Io has never stored a card number
